question: Which of the following correctly identifies a distinguishing feature of Anopheles mosquitoes compared to Culex and Aedes?

answers.text: Anopheles larvae lie parallel to the water surface; adults rest with the body at an angle to the surface

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Anopheles larvae float horizontally (parallel), and adults adopt a characteristic head-down, tail-up angle when resting — both are key identification features.

answers.text: Anopheles larvae hang perpendicular to the water surface via a siphon tube

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hanging perpendicular via a siphon is characteristic of Culex and Aedes larvae, not Anopheles.

answers.text: Anopheles adults rest with the body parallel to the surface (horizontal)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Anopheles adults rest at an angle (body tilted toward the surface), not horizontally. Culex adults rest with the body parallel.

answers.text: Anopheles females do not take blood meals

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both male and female Anopheles feed on plant nectar, but only female Anopheles take blood meals for egg maturation and transmit malaria.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key distinction: Anopheles larvae float parallel to the water surface (no siphon), and adults rest at a head-down angle to the surface. Culex and Aedes larvae hang perpendicular.
Correct! Anopheles larvae float parallel to the water surface, and adults rest at a characteristic head-down angle — mnemonically, 'Ano = angle'.
